title: The miqat, where pilgrims begin
hookLine: pilgrims enter ihram at set points around Mecca
carry: at the miqat, a traveler becomes a pilgrim

lines: THE AIRCRAFT WILL SOON PASS THE POINT.
cards: Somewhere over the desert, on the way into Jeddah, a plane full of pilgrims gets an announcement: the aircraft will soon pass the point.

Up and down the aisles, people who boarded in ordinary clothes are already changed, or changing in the cramped bathrooms, or quietly saying the words that mark the start. Nothing on the ground below looks different.
There's no gate, no fence, no sign you could see from the window. But the line is there, and they know it.

teach.h: WHERE THE TRAVELER BECOMES A PILGRIM.
teach.b: First, what a miqat is: a set point, a boundary place, where pilgrims heading for Mecca enter ihram, the sacred state of the pilgrimage. Before it, a person is a traveler.
Past it, for Hajj or umrah, they must already be a pilgrim. Second, who set them.

A hadith from Ibn Abbas in Sahih al-Bukhari names the places: Dhul Hulayfah for the people of Medina; al-Juhfah for the people of Sham, the lands to the north; Qarn al-Manazil for the people of Najd; Yalamlam for the people of Yemen.
Other reports add a point for the people of Iraq. And the points are for the people of those lands and for anyone else who passes through them on the way to Hajj or umrah.
Whoever lives closer enters ihram from where they are, and the people of Mecca from Mecca itself. Third, why a line at all.

teach.h: THE LINE MEETS YOU ON YOUR ROAD.
teach.b: The places sit at different distances from Mecca, out on the roads people actually traveled, so the boundary meets each traveler on their own road.
Nobody walks into the sacred state by accident, and nobody slips past it unnoticed.
Hence the plane announcement: scholars hold that the old points still apply in the air, so pilgrims enter ihram as they cross them, or before. Fourth, the word.

teach.h: A SET PLACE, AN APPOINTED TIME.
teach.b: Miqat also carries the sense of an appointed time. In surah seven, when Musa comes to his meeting with his Lord on the mountain, the Qur'an uses this same word for that appointed meeting.
A place and a time, both set in advance, both kept. The miqat is where an ordinary journey becomes a pilgrimage.

how: Pilgrims enter ihram at or before the miqat on their route; some flying in change into ihram before boarding or on the plane, and airlines may announce when the miqat is near.

games.q: you're flying to Mecca for umrah. the plane is about to pass over the miqat. what do pilgrims do?
o: wait until they land and enter ihram at the hotel.
enter ihram before the plane passes the point.
skip ihram; it only applies on foot.

practice: Bring to mind a doorway you cross every day without noticing: your front door, the door to your work, the door of your car.
Picture yourself pausing there for one breath before you step through, the way a pilgrim knows the point is coming. What would you want to leave outside, and what would you want to carry in?
